articles.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur has won a lot, but will it be enough if he can't take the next step?
articles.summary: Matt LaFleur has won a lot of games. To some, it hasn't been enough.
articles.body:
Matt LaFleur's win percentage puts him in elite company. His 65.4% mark is tied for 16th all time . It's better than Bill Belichick's career mark of 64.7%.

But maybe that's not good enough for Green Bay Packers fans.

There were questions late last season if LaFleur was coaching for his job . As the Packers faltered following Micah Parsons' injury , speculation grew . That ultimately didn't matter. Despite the Packers losing their last five games, including two blown leads to the Chicago Bears, LaFleur signed a multi-year extension in January .

Still, if the Packers fail to make the playoffs this season, would LaFleur be on the hot seat? The fact that it's even a topic says something about the lack of patience in the NFL.

Just because media and fans speculate on a successful coach being in trouble doesn't mean he is. The Packers aren't an impulsive organization. Despite the embarrassing losses to the Bears, which included blowing a 21-3 halftime lead in a wild-card round loss, Packers president Ed Policy said he never considered firing LaFleur.

"Frankly, the fact that I was being asked, 'Is firing him even an option at that point?' I was a little bit shocked by that," Packers president Ed Policy said .

That's reasonable. LaFleur's worst season in seven years as Packers coach is 8-9. He has made the playoffs six times in that stretch. He has had that success with two different quarterbacks, Aaron Rodgers and Jordan Love. It hasn't resulted in a Super Bowl appearance, but plenty of franchises would love to make the playoffs six times in seven seasons.

LaFleur has been successful. Just not successful enough to escape questions about his job security .

The NFL, on the whole, has become impatient. That's why there are 10 new head coaches this season, which ties a league record. It is becoming increasingly rare for a coach to get three or more seasons if there's not instant success. In reality, only a few head coaches aren't on the hot seat. It seems all but the top tier are a bad season away from answering the same questions LaFleur was late last season. And LaFleur hasn't even had a terrible season.

But LaFleur also hasn't had a Super Bowl season. There have been memorable losses in the biggest moments. In LaFleur's first three seasons the Packers were a No. 2 seed once and a No. 1 seed twice and didn't make the Super Bowl in any of those seasons. There were heartbreaking losses late in playoff games against the 49ers three seasons ago and the Bears last season. The repeated disappointments have led to the criticisms. This season has challenges already too, with Parsons out for the first few games as he rehabs from his knee injury and Josh Jacobs being placed on the commissioner's exempt list.

That's life for an NFL head coach. By most measures LaFleur has won more often than not only most of his peers but most coaches through NFL history. But he also has stalled in the playoffs. A pair of brutal losses to the Packers' archrival from Chicago didn't slow down the angst toward him.

In another era, there would never be a question about LaFleur's job security. He would have bought himself at least enough job security to survive a non-playoff season or two. This NFL is unforgiving. That's how you go from winning nearly two-thirds of your games to open speculation that you're on the hot seat.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ private message to a grieving Chiefs reporter revealed after father’s sudden death
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has once again shown a softer side away from the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback reportedly reached out privately t.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has once again shown a softer side away from the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback reportedly reached out privately to a Chiefs media member following the unexpected death of his father, offering a message of support during a devastating family loss.Patrick Mahomes’ private words to grieving Chiefs reporter revealed after heartbreaking lossThe media member, Tucker Franklin, shared that his father, Doug Franklin, had died unexpectedly. In the aftermath of the tragedy, Mahomes personally sent Franklin a message offering his condolences and letting him know that the Chiefs community was behind him.“Praying for your family man. Chiefs and Chief Kingdom is with you!” Mahomes wrote, according to Franklin.mFor Franklin, the gesture appeared to mean far more than a simple message from an NFL superstar.He later shared Mahomes’ words publicly, reflecting on the fact that the quarterback he has covered and supported was taking the time to reach out during one of the most difficult moments of his life.The moment also offered a glimpse into the relationship between Mahomes and the Kansas City media community, where the quarterback has spent years surrounded by reporters covering his remarkable Chiefs career.But this time, there was no football headline, game-winning throw, or postgame celebration. There was simply a grieving son and a quarterback offering support.Mahomes has become accustomed to enormous attention whenever he steps onto the field. Every touchdown, loss, and playoff run can become national news. Yet moments like this happen far away from the cameras. And Franklin’s decision to reveal the message gave fans a rare look at that side of Mahomes.The loss of a parent is deeply personal, and Franklin did not simply receive a message from one of the NFL’s biggest stars; he received a reminder that the Chiefs organization and its wider community were standing with him.For Chiefs Kingdom, it was another reason to see Mahomes as more than just the face of the franchise. On the field, he is one of football’s biggest stars.Off it, his private gesture to a grieving member of the Chiefs media community offered a much quieter and more personal moment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seahawks' top challenger on road to Super Bowl defense should be the Rams. But with more than 100 days until that test, Patriots arrive first
articles.summary: So while the Patriots stand first on the Seahawks' schedule for a Super Bowl rematch, the team far more pertinent to Seattle's road back to the biggest stage...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks will remember where they were on Feb. 8, when they won the Super Bowl.

Many in the club will also remember where they were on June 1.

"It was a bad day," general manager John Schneider told Yahoo Sports during a recent training camp practice. "It was a really bad day."

Because on June 1, the Seahawks' division-rival Los Angeles Rams traded for Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. The Rams, whom the Seahawks outlasted by four points in the NFC championship, now field both the reigning DPOY and the reigning MVP in quarterback Matthew Stafford.

The Rams acquired veteran cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in the spring in a move many framed as set to stop Seahawks receiver and reigning receiving yards champion Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

And last week, in a move Smith-Njigba said "definitely went around the building," the Rams welcomed back three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald.

So while the New England Patriots stand first on the Seahawks' schedule for a Super Bowl rematch, the team far more pertinent to Seattle's road back to the biggest stage has been loading up loudly and repeatedly.

The Seahawks-Rams rivalry that captivated fans last year should reach a whole new tenor this year.

And yet: The teams will not play the first of their two division games until Dec. 25 — 107 days after the Seahawks' season opener.

So when asked about game-planning for Garrett and the newly loaded Rams, first-year Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was ready.

"I've been waiting for somebody to ask me this question," he told Yahoo Sports on Aug. 13. "And you may or may not like my answer.

"If you want to talk to somebody about Christmas in August, you should be talking to my wife. She's Christmas shopping right now."

Christmas will not come in September or October, so instead consider the Seahawks eager to test their 2026 identity against the Patriots on Wednesday.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald has preached a mindset of "run it forward" rather than "run it back" as Seattle chases a title defense. Smith-Njigba doesn't worry about his team's patience.

"It's very tough in this league to look ahead that far and to be antsy for one team when you have the Patriots, when you have the Broncos and the Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers," he told Yahoo Sports last week . "This league is just very challenging and we preach the process. So it wouldn't be us to look too much forward into that game. …

"That's a game we are looking forward to, but you just have to control it and just get ready for Week 1. The Patriots, they bring on a big challenge."

Drake Maye on Seahawks: 'Revenge game, but I would not say revenge game'

Even with a consecutive-game rematch, Macdonald cautions his team about relying too much on a scouting report from February to strategize a game in September.

"You don't want to fall in the trap of applying last year's things that you see too much to what's going to happen this year," Macdonald told reporters. "Teams grow and evolve and change, and there's different personnel on both sides."

The mantra of change is a favorite among Macdonald and Vrabel as each tries to streamline the emotions that could accompany the Seahawks' banner-raising just before kickoff. But in reality: There's not been wholesale change in either franchise. The Seahawks, in particular, will look very similar to their Super Bowl outfit when they take the field Wednesday.

Twenty of the Seahawks' 22 Super Bowl starters remain on their roster this season, only running back Kenneth Walker III and defensive back Coby Bryant leaving in free agency to the Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears, respectively.

The Patriots return most starters but have more change: Six Super Bowl starters have left to other teams, including four defenders. And that count does not include the departure of receivers Stefon Diggs (Washington Commanders) and Kayshon Boutte (Houston Texans), who did not start in the Super Bowl but played 63% and 73% of offensive snaps, respectively.

Free agency acquisitions shifted rosters as did each teams' draft classes. But each team returns primarily starters from the emotion-laden big stage. Could that impact the NFL's season opener, which has featured a Super Bowl rematch just one other time (2016) since 1970?

"You like to think it's a new year," Patriots quarterback Drake Maye told reporters. "You like to think that but at the same time, you [will] go against an opponent that you just lost a Super Bowl against. In the last game that I played and was out there, we lost to them in the biggest game. That's why you play the game …

"So there's definitely, I would not say 'extra,' [but] just a little bit of, 'Man, this is our chance to start the season off strong on a good foot and knowing that the opportunity that we have, you get a little bit of a — you get your revenge game, but I would not say revenge game.

"They won the big one, and we got to start the season off. You cannot get that game back that we lost, so we are onto something new."

The Seahawks appear to have fewer Super Bowl-related emotions invested in the outcome of the game, players and coaches emphasizing their desire to win to establish a foundation for this season but not their desire to win because of the implications of their opponent.

Macdonald said "it hasn't really been a topic of conversation" given the "long time between the two games" of teams who are now "different versions of who we are."

The Seahawks, at home and bearing rings, are 3.5-point betting favorites .

"We're the champs, so it's like, why would we put emphasis on that?" defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence told Yahoo Sports. "They can do what they want to do. But we the champs and they still have to come to our house and see how we get down."

What changes should Seahawks, Patriots most expect?

How, exactly, will the Seahawks get down?

While Seattle may not be emphasizing the emotional element of the Week 1 rematch, the strategic elements of the game's timing is relevant.

Coaches and players across the league refer to early-season contests as a game of "unscouted looks." With roster shifts and months of schematic tweaking, the number of plays and personnel groupings that opponents won't expect tends to peak during the opening week of the NFL season.

Macdonald's response: a training camp heavy on situational work.

Two-minute and four-minute drills canvassed Seattle's practices, the defensive-minded Macdonald creating so many unideal situations for Fleury as he adapted to calling plays that Fleury joked he wondered who kept burning through all of his timeouts. Coaches would receive a batch of situations late the night before practice or the morning of, Fleury said. Four-minute work would bleed immediately into two-minute work without time to regroup.

"It's irritating in the moment, but it's necessary at the same time," Fleury said. "Every single day is a different scenario."

That situational focus from Macdonald has helped the Seahawks in recent years, players and coaches said. Defensive coordinator Aden Durde remembered a game in which they practiced and discussed a situation that went on to unfold just so in the week's game. Durde declined to give specifics on the situation.

"But it actually happened and we won the game," Durde told Yahoo Sports. "It was an NFC West game. I don't think it's my place to say [which]."

For now, the biggest post-February change the Seahawks' defense must prepare for is the Patriots' trade for receiver A.J. Brown, giving Maye perhaps his surest target yet alongside free-agent signing Romeo Doubs. Seattle's offense would be wise to heed the Patriots' acquisition of cornerback Kevin Byard, whose seven interceptions last season led the NFL.

And while Seattle's defensive innovation must stem more from Macdonald's schematic evolution than from personnel changes, Seattle's run game could look significantly different. Walker left in free agency for the Chiefs after earning Super Bowl MVP honors for his 135 rushing yards and 161 total scrimmage yards to pace the 29-13 win.

Seahawks veteran running back Zach Charbonnet remains on the physically unable to perform list to start the NFL season after tearing his ACL in Seattle's NFC divisional-round game.

The Seahawks drafted running back Jadarian Price with the final pick of the first round in April.

During training camp, coaches and teammates touted Price's speed getting to the perimeter and patience in moving as well as his shifting between speeds to catch defenders in off angles. Price stood out to them in the passing game with his feel for space and explosiveness as well as his vision in the running game.

None of that ensures he'll be ready to carry a Walker-like load in Week 1.

"He's doing as well as any rookie I've ever been with, but he's still a rookie," Fleury said. "And so there's no substitute for learning through experience. He's immensely, very sharp. He's learning what he's supposed to do, but not necessarily how he's supposed to do it and what some of the real-time reactions to the other side of the ball are.

"That's just going to happen with time and reps and experience in games at full speed."

Health permitting, Price should have ample opportunity to gain reps and experience before the Seahawks at least see the Rams on Dec. 25 — and again, for their regular-season finale, on Jan. 10.

By then, the Rams' ceiling with Garrett, Donald and their new cornerbacks will be clearer. That bad day from June when Garrett was traded from the AFC North to the NFC West will be further removed. How much Donald has left in the tank will be more evident, too.

"It [was] a competitive division without him," Smith-Njigba said of Donald. "He's someone that you have to account for and we're going to do our best to maintain and to try to stop him. But we're accepting the challenge. We're going to accept the challenge each week, go in with a great game plan and execute. And I truly believe that.

"Whatever may come our way, we'll be ready for it."

articles.title: Patriots' CB Christian Gonzalez reportedly signs record-setting 4-year, $135 million extension
articles.summary: Christian Gonzalez was an All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler last season.
articles.body:
Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots have agreed on a four-year, $135 million extension late on Monday night, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

The 24-year-old is now the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL and the highest-paid player in Patriots history. Defensive lineman Milton Williams owned the record previously after signing a four-year, $104 million ($63 million guaranteed) deal during free agency in March 2025.

Top 10 NFL CB Salaries (Average annual value)

Gonzalez is now one of two cornerbacks in NFL history to reach a deal worth more than $130 million. Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year, $132 million extension last month, which briefly made him the highest-paid player at the position.

The Patriots appeared to confirm the new deal on social media on Monday night.

A second-team All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler last season, Gonzalez was the Patriots' first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. After playing only four games during his rookie season due to a torn labrum and dislocated shoulder, he suited up 16 times in 2024, recording 50 solo tackles and two interceptions.

Gonzalez didn't play until Week 4 last season due to a hamstring injury suffered in preseason. He ended up appearing in 14 regular-season games and made a career-high 69 total tackles and 10 pass deflections. During the Patriots' run to Super Bowl LX, he made a game-clinching interception off Denver Broncos quarterback Jarrett Stidham late in the fourth quarter of the AFC championship game.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft revealed on the first day of training camp that the team had offered the cornerback a record-setting extension.

"We love Christian Gonzalez," Kraft said. "We love him as a player, as a person. That's why we've made an offer to him that makes him the highest-paid player ever to play that position in the NFL, and coincidentally, it's the highest contract in the Patriots' franchise history. So we're glad we drafted him and we developed here, and we hope he'll be with us for a long time."

Gonzalez is entering his fourth NFL season and was eligible to sign an extension on his rookie contract. The Patriots picked up his fifth-year option in the offseason, and the Oregon product reported to training camp as negotiations were ongoing.

With the Patriots opening the new season Wednesday night in Seattle, the two sides got Gonzalez's deal done just in time.

articles.title: Myles Garrett, Patrick Mahomes and Jesse Minter: The NFL's biggest storylines on road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season kicks off on Wednesday night when the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots, live on Sky Sports from 1.20am in the early hours of Thursday; Super Bowl 61 takes place at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Sunday February 14
articles.body:
The new campaign begins on Wednesday night when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks take on the New England Patriots, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am in the early hours of Thursday.

The phrase 'all in' can be over-exhausted at times in the NFL, but rarely has it been as glaringly-fitting than in the case of the 2026 Los Angeles Rams. They made the biggest move of the offseason by acquiring reigning Defensive Player of the Year and generational pass rusher Myles Garrett in a blockbuster trade with the Cleveland Browns, traded for Kansas City Chiefs star cornerback Trent McDuffie, reunited him with free agent corner Jaylen Watson and welcomed back Aaron Donald as the three-time Defensive Player of the Year came out of retirement to forge one of the most frightening defensive tandems in NFL history alongside Garrett.

Stop them and there is already an existing core of Byron Young, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske and chess piece safety Quentin Lake for which to account.

They enter the season led by reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback, have one of the league's most talented wide receivers in Puka Nacua, boast an upper-tier rushing attack of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum and just produced the NFL's most potent offense on the way to the NFC Championship Game last year, where they fell short against the champion Seattle Seahawks in a game more Super Bowl-esque than the Super Bowl itself. They are favourites for a reason.

The Baltimore Ravens are desperate to cash in on the prime of their generational quarterback, and so moved on from head coach John Harbaugh after 18 seasons this year in view of a fresh look to their Super Bowl charge. They would turn to former Los Angeles Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter and former Chicago Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle as the men to help Lamar Jackson lead the Ravens over the line following a playoff-less campaign on the back of three Divisional Round exits and an AFC Championship Game defeat in six seasons.

Between Jackson, Derrick Henry and Doyle's offensive scheme, the Ravens have the potential to be one of the league's most destructive play-action run-heavy attacks. Questions remain of a receiving core spearheaded by Zay Flowers, but there are high expectations for third-round rookie Ja'Kobi Lane.

A slow start and marquee injuries, namely to Jackson himself, cost Baltimore in 2025, so too one of the worst pass defenses in football. Minter had been instrumental in transforming the Chargers' defense during his time alongside Harbaugh, and arrives armed with the personnel to orchestrate one of the league's best units behind all-action safety Kyle Hamilton, a returning Nnamdi Madubuike and offseason addition Trey Hendrickson.

Despite his demise in Miami, former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel remains one of football's most prized offensive architects as he takes his expertise over to California. There he has been tasked with unlocking the best of Justin Herbert as the new offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Chargers, whose franchise quarterback is yet to shake the monkey of a first career playoff win off his back. For all the blockbuster arm talent, Herbert's chief criticism remains his modest postseason record, but McDaniel and his whacky wizardry is in town to change that.

It remains a team somewhat built on 'ifs' as far as their AFC West challenge is concerned. 'If' star offensive tackle tandem Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater can rediscover their best after combining for just six games due to injury last season, 'if' running back Omarion Hampton can be a difference-maker, 'if' Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston is enough firepower for Herbert on the outside, 'if' first-round pick Akheem Mesidor can make an immediate impact to a slightly understaffed pass rush, 'if' Tuli Tuipulotu, Derwin James and a 35-year-old Khalil Mack can preserve Minter's influence with last season's top-10 defense.

Herbert is a freak, but he is not immune to queries, and this is his best chance yet to firmly nestle himself among the AFC's perennial contenders.

It was a strange 2025 season in Philly, where the Eagles clinched the NFC East division title amid a storm of locker room tension and frequent offensive sputters during the defence of their Super Bowl title. It would culminate in a wild-card round defeat to the San Francisco 49ers and the eventual departure of wantaway wide receiver AJ Brown, who appeared to drift from quarterback Jalen Hurts while being critical of Kevin Patullo's play-calling within an attack that slumped to 24th in total yards.

Patullo was fired as offensive coordinator this offseason and replaced by former Green Bay Packers quarterback coach Sean Mannion, who will turn to DeVonta Smith as his No 1 passing threat along with a new supporting cast of Hollywood Brown, Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon in the Eagles' bid to adapt to life without Brown.

Legendary coach Jeff Stoutland retired this offseason, but leaves what remains one of the league's most accomplished offensive lines. Behind it sits Saquon Barkley, whose cut exploits should thrive in Mannion's outside zone plant-and-go scheme as he responds to a perceived 'down' year. On the opposite side of the ball Vic Fangio still pulls the strings to one of the most talent-rich personnel groups among NFL defenses, for which there appears zero concerns. All eyes turn to the Hurts and Mannion marriage.

The Kansas City Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season on the back of reaching seven straight AFC Championship games and five Super Bowls in six campaigns, three of which they won. It was also the first time since 2015 that they failed to win the AFC West, slumping to third with a record of 6-11 as offensive frailties finally caught up with them. To make matters worse quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending torn ACL and LCL in December, for which he underwent immediate surgery. He is back - but how back? And are THEY back?

Andy Reid's dynasty men had found themselves in a rare place on the periphery, Mahomes enduring his worst statistical campaign and a once high-powered attack finally fizzling out into nothingness having long-been rescued by Steve Spagnuolo's defense. You would be hard pushed arguing Mahomes is not still the NFL's best quarterback, and hard pushed believing he will not wrestle back his command of the league at some stage, but the Chiefs await to see just how quickly he can get back to being the same dynamic out-of-structure menace in the wake of his recovery.

Travis Kelce is not the same defining wrinkle to Reid's playbook at the age of 36, while Rashee Rice faces a 'prove it' year as Mahomes' lead receiver after playing just eight games in 2025. The Chiefs did, though, seek to ease their quarterback's return by signing Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III as a new dimension to an uninspiring backfield, while replacing Matt Nagy with returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, a popular figure in their past Super Bowl success. A Mahomes, Reid and Spagnuolo trio might, meanwhile, still be the best in football.

Sean Payton's Championship-contender Denver Broncos will not give up the AFC West easily, though.

Joe Burrow insists he is tired of waiting, tired of kicking Cincinnati's Super Bowl can down the road, tired of saying 'next time'; for him, this is it, the chance to get back to the 'Big Dance', the chance to win it all. Rarely do you doubt his confidence, rarely do you not believe in his ability to lift a Lombardi, but between injuries, including to Burrow himself, and roster imbalance the Bengals have never quite worked it out since falling at the final hurdle against the Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

They have now missed the playoffs in three straight seasons, an astonishing mini-drought considering that, behind Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can be one of the most explosive aerial attacks in football.

An apparent move towards more play-action and under-center looks is a fascinating and long-coveted wrinkle to a Bengals offense criticised for becoming stale at times under Zac Taylor. In truth, though, it has never really been deficiencies on offense to prompt their struggles, but instead their consistent issues on defense. They just traded a first-round pick for Dexter Lawrence and acquired edge rusher Boye Mafe - but is it enough?

'Run it forward' was the term used by Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald this offseason as Seattle prepare to defend their Super Bowl crown following February's dominant win over the New England Patriots. And there is no reason they cannot map out a route back to February's finale.

Kenneth Walker's exit raises some fresh uncertainty in the backfield, but this is still a complete roster brimming with playmakers and overseen by perhaps the top defensive mastermind in the league currently. Sam Darnold is coming off a season in which he performed like a top-10 quarterback to shun critics for good, feeding Jaxon Smith-Njigba on his way to a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards.

Macdonald and Aden Durde's defense, meanwhile, ranked first in EPA per drive and first in points allowed with little evidence of a decline threat. Besides Walker and the addition of rookie running back Jadarian Price, the one sizeable change comes on the sidelines as Brian Fleury takes over play-calling duties for the first time following offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak's departure to become head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Nonetheless, another Super Bowl run is on the cards.

It feels like a different story in New England, where you cannot help but brace for the possibility of regression for a Patriots team that flew ahead of schedule by reaching the Super Bowl. It would end in a humbling defeat to a far greater Seahawks team, but that should not deter from Drake Maye announcing himself as a long-term solution to the Patriots' quarterback problems. He reaped the rewards of daring to be the most aggressive passer in football, and the Patriots provided him with much-needed perimeter depth this offseason by welcoming AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs.

TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson are capable of joining the best rushing attacks in the league, Christian Gonzalez is an elite cornerstone on a defense that ranked eighth in yards and fourth in points, but there are still concerns in the trenches over a lack of star quality to their pass rush and an offensive line that allowed 47 sacks last year.

Nothing underlines the Mahomes and Reid effect quite like the sight of the Buffalo Bills firing Sean McDermott, the Baltimore Ravens parting with Harbaugh and Burrow's call for urgency to the Cincinnati Bengals' Super Bowl push. Granted, Mahomes and Reid did not dump any of them out last season, but it is for Kansas City's dynasty dominance that the agony of all three has been prolonged, particularly in the case of Josh Allen and the Bills.

Much like Jackson in Baltimore, the Bills have a responsibility to maximise the best of their alien quarterback, behind whom they have been banging on the Super Bowl door. They are nursing the wounds of fresh playoff disappointment after suffering an overtime loss to the Broncos to mark their fourth divisional-round defeat in the last five years, as much prompting the end of McDermott's reign. Joe Brady was subsequently promoted to head coach while Jim Leonhard was hired as Buffalo's new defensive coordinator in the organisation's bid to get over the line.

For as long as Allen is healthy and on the field, the Bills will remain Super Bowl contenders. There is a strong case for him being the league's most defining 'X factor' such has become his ability to strap an entire team to his back while combining for the most total touchdowns by any quarterback since entering the league in 2018. It is for him, with the help of last season's league rushing leader James Cook, that the Bills rarely stray from a place at the top of offensive rankings.

This year's marquee addition is wide receiver DJ Moore, while the major interest lies with a new-look defense that introduces Bradley Chubb and CJ Gardner-Johnson following something of an exodus including Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White.

Liam Coen and Ben Johnson both issued a warning of new contenders to the rest of the league during impressive maiden seasons as the respective head coaches of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears, each punching a ticket to the playoffs and each finding joy with their No 1-pick quarterbacks. Will they take the next step?

Trevor Lawrence delivered the most clinical, most commanding year of his Jags career by a distance as he threw for 4,007 yards and 29 touchdowns to 12 interceptions while also rushing for nine scores on the way to the wild-card round, where Coen's side were eventually stopped by the Buffalo Bills. It featured an eight-game winning streak to finish the campaign as the Jags' offense took flight alongside an Anthony Campanile that ranked fifth in EPA/play. Questions come in a backfield that just lost its chief rushing threat in Travis Etienne, making for a new-look committee attack led by Bhayshul Tuten.

Elsewhere, Johnson lived up to his billing as one of the most exciting modern offensive minds in football as he won 11 games in his first year while taking the Bears to the divisional-round of the playoffs. He conjured one of the most dynamic rushing schemes in the league and proved the perfect coach to put Caleb Williams in positions to succeed, cutting down on the negative plays and embracing his proclivity for the spectacular. Sure, accuracy inconsistencies are still under the microscope, but the makings of a formidable coach-quarterback tandem are there. Chicago's bigger concern is perhaps its shortage of pass rush threats.

Will the Cowboys and Texans make elite units count?

Only the Los Angeles Rams flaunted a more potent offense than the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 as a triple-threat of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens through the air was complemented by long-awaited rushing success thanks largely to Javonte Williams.

The stunning decision to trade away Micah Parsons was, meanwhile, followed by the Cowboys' defense ranking third-worst in yards allowed, worst against the pass, and worst in points allowed. It became a point of focus this offseason as the Cowboys hired Christian Parker as their new defensive coordinator, traded for former Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Rashan Gary and spent the 11th overall pick on safety Caleb Downs. Even a middle-of-the-road defense would be enough to put this team in contention, with Dak an outside MVP candidate and the Lamb-Pickens receiver axis as frightening as perhaps any in football.

It was a contrasting tale in Houston as DeMeco Ryans' Texans defense tormented the league while ranking No 1 in yards allowed, second in scoring and second in EPA/play. Will Anderson Jr and Danielle Hunter were unplayable up front, while Derek Stingley cemented his status as a premium lock-down corner at the core of a dogged, hard-nosed, suffocating unit that would led their side's route to the divisional round of the playoffs.

The attention turns to CJ Stroud amid contract negotiations with the quarterback, who threw four interceptions in the postseason loss to New England having not quite built on his emphatic rookie campaign as many had anticipated. The offensive line had been a contributing factor as one of Houston's glaring weaknesses, general manager Nick Caserio seeking to strengthen protection for Stroud by adding Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith and first-round rookie Keylan Rutledge. He also traded for running back David Montgomery as added juice to an attack ranked 18th in yards, and 22nd in rushing last season.

In another life Kyler Murray would/might/should be one of the most talked about epitomes of footballing escapism such is the talent of a quarterback joystick with the arm and wheels to wreak havoc. It has been nothing short of a slog and a disappointing chapter of irrelevance since the marquee contract featuring his widely-ridiculed homework clause in Arizona, but he enters the 2026 season as perhaps the most high-profile resurrection candidate.

Murray turned the page on his career this offseason as he signed with the Minnesota Vikings, teaming up with a head coach in Kevin O'Connell famed for his quarterback-whispering qualities, evidenced through Sam Darnold's career rebound.

Murray has swiftly ousted JJ McCarthy as the starting quarterback and will now take the reins on an offense led by the league's best receiver in Justin Jefferson, accompanied by a talented cast of Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and TJ Hockenson.

Murray is among the most intriguing case studies as he seeks to revive his career within the most gifted cohort of weapons and coaches he has experienced since being selected as the No 1 pick in 2019. That includes an 'X factor' of a defensive coordinator in Brian Flores who continues to roll out one of football's most inventive, full throttle, blitz-heavy units.

Watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every London game, Thanksgiving and every minute of the playoffs on the road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles.

articles.title: NFL 2026 Predictions: Who will reach Super Bowl? Who will win NFL MVP?
articles.summary: Who are favourites to reach the Super Bowl and who will be the surprise standouts? BBC's NFL experts make their predictions for the 2026 season - and so can you.
articles.body:
The NFL is notoriously difficult to predict and last season was no different.

Seven of the eight division winners were different from 2024, with two of the Super Bowl favourites missing out on the play-offs entirely - the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs.

Two outsiders then made it all the way to the big game, with the Seattle Seahawks beating the New England Patriots for their first NFL championship in 12 years.

So, who will be this season's surprise package? Who will be playing at Super Bowl 61 next February? And who will be the main men?

Here, the BBC's NFL experts make their picks for the 2026 season, which begins this week. Plus you can predict your Super Bowl winner at the bottom of this page.

Rob Staton: I think the NFC will be another battle between the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks. I'm going to go with the Rams, simply because only two teams have repeated since the turn of the century. I have them facing the Buffalo Bills. Josh Allen finally gets to the big game.

Hugh Ferris: You could argue that, aside from an underwhelming head coach hire, there's little reason the 2026 Bills will be any different to the recent incarnations. I'm picking them to finally get over the line, though, and reach the Super Bowl, but to lose nonetheless. It's incredibly difficult to choose anyone else rather than the Rams, isn't it?

Haydn Parry: Surely the Bills can convert Allen's talent and make it to the season showpiece? Joe Brady's promotion to head coach might prove to be the missing ingredient. From the NFC, I think the Rams look most likely to have a strong tilt this campaign, and I see them winning it.

Joe Bradshaw: The last time the Super Bowl was at SoFi Stadium in 2022, the Rams won on home territory and they look primed to repeat next February. From the AFC, surely Bills quarterback Allen is overdue a trip to the NFL's biggest game, even if it will ultimately end in defeat.

David Brindle: After losing Bo Nix to injury in last season's play-offs, I expect the Denver Broncos to use that as motivation and at least go one further this season. As for the Rams, it's very difficult to look past the consensus predictions for the Super Bowl.

Ben Collins: Full disclosure, I'd seen the above before writing this so here's some leftfield picks... imagine if it's the Los Angeles Chargers that actually get to play in the Super Bowl in their own stadium, and it's former Rams quarterback Jared Goff that leads Detroit to victory.

Rob Staton: I'm going with Josh Allen . He now has an offensive-minded head coach running the team. Everything will be geared towards him having a big season.

Hugh Ferris: In an attempt to think outside the box, I'm picking Justin Herbert of the Chargers. You might suggest a quarterback in a Jim Harbaugh team isn't likely to get the chance to have an MVP-level season, but the hiring of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator might change that.

Haydn Parry: I might be wearing my blue-star goggles here but Dak Prescott has the ability and the weapons to have an outstanding season. Offence was not the Dallas Cowboys' problem last year and it certainly wasn't Prescott's fault that the team failed to deliver. Dallas just need to find a 'D'.

Joe Bradshaw: Buffalo's new head coach Joe Brady has stepped up from offensive coordinator so knows how to get Josh Allen purring. If the Bills make the Super Bowl, their quarterback will be the obvious candidate for his second MVP award.

David Brindle: If it wasn't to be a quarterback, I fancy Jahmyr Gibbs . He's signed a new deal and now has no running back competition at Detroit so expect him to see lots of action on a Lions team who are NFC contenders.

Ben Collins: Cincinnati have remedied their defence and still have a top offence. After twice winning comeback player of the year, quarterback Joe Burrow stays fit long enough to bag the award he really wants as the Bengals make a deep play-off run.

Rob Staton: It could be Joe Brady if he can help Josh Allen reach MVP status, but in order to mix things up I'm going for DeMeco Ryans . The Houston Texans are going to lead on their defence and I think they'll be really strong.

Hugh Ferris: If the Bills reach the Super Bowl, then it stands to reason Joe Brady gets the nod as a first-year head coach, putting to shame people (like me) who called him an underwhelming hire.

Haydn Parry: I have always been a big fan of John Harbaugh . He will start from a comparatively low base in New York with the Giants, but with their passionate fanbase and the enormous potential of Jaxson Dart lift-off could be achieved early.

Joe Bradshaw: There has been such turnover on the NFL's coaching carousel, it has been hard to keep up this off-season. In the face of such instability, I'll opt for Sean McVay as he steers the Rams to their third Super Bowl title.

David Brindle: I'm going for Sean Payton to pick up his second award, 20 years after winning it with New Orleans. With the work done so far and decisions Payton has already made at Denver, this is the year I think it'll be formally recognised.

Ben Collins: After Detroit were hindered by a defensive injury crisis last season, Dan Campbell is rewarded as he gets the Lions roaring again.

Rob Staton: I'd expect Rueben Bain to have an immediate impact in Tampa Bay. Jadarian Price will get opportunities to shine in Seattle. I was a big fan of De'Zhaun Stribling, taken by the San Francisco 49ers. But in terms of pure impact, give me Caleb Downs , the safety in Dallas.

Hugh Ferris: The 49ers have one wide receiver AWOL, another out for the season, and injury question marks over Mike Evans and George Kittle - who's recovering from a torn Achilles - so along with a returning Deebo Samuel, there's a gap for De'Zhaun Stribling to fill.

Haydn Parry: It will be interesting to see how wide receiver Carnell Tate , fourth overall pick by Tennessee, adapts among the big boys. With his versatile skillset, the Titans expect him to contribute right from the off - the pre-draft scout reports highlighted his maturity, intelligence, sure hands and catch radius.

Joe Bradshaw: De'Zhaun Stribling was a surprise selection by the 49ers at the start of the second round but given their annual injury issues, he could be in line for plenty of work this season. Some fine displays in pre-season have only increased the hype.

David Brindle: After Kenneth Walker departed, the Seahawks picked Jadarian Price in the draft. He'll start the season as their lead back, with Zach Charbonnet still recovering from an ACL tear. I expect him to keep that job and become a top running back in the league for many years.

Ben Collins: Sonny Styles' athleticism caught the eye of NFL teams during the pre-draft process. He could have a big impact at linebacker for the Washington Commanders and soon become one of their leaders.

Rob Staton: I'm not suggesting the Las Vegas Raiders are going to go on an improbable run or anything, but Klint Kubiak did an excellent job in Seattle [as offensive coordinator] and should make the transition to head coach with ease. I think this will be the year, finally, that the Raiders show signs of growth.

Hugh Ferris: Here's a surprise: the New York teams won't both be terrible. The Jets' draft and John Harbaugh going to the Giants should mean they could rise to the heady heights of being mediocre.

Haydn Parry: Fernando Mendoza worked wonders at Indiana last year. He probably needs to perform miracles in Las Vegas but it will be fascinating to follow his progress. The lad needs broad shoulders to carry the weight of expectation but the Raiders can hardly do worse than last season.

Joe Bradshaw: Can you call a team with consecutive 11-win seasons a surprise package? Despite great regular seasons, the Los Angeles Chargers have faltered in the play-offs but they are now healthy again and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel looks a perfect fit for talented quarterback Justin Herbert.

David Brindle: Given they missed the play-offs and went 6-11 last season, if the Cincinnati Bengals can stay healthy - especially quarterback Joe Burrow, who missed most of last season with turf toe - they could reach the Super Bowl and upset the status quo.

Ben Collins: Kevin Stefanski was twice named coach of the year at Cleveland and now has a more stable team at his disposal in Atlanta, led by dual-threat running back Bijan Robinson. If the Falcons can settle on a quarterback, they could finally get back in play-off contention.

Which team will have NFL's worst record?

Rob Staton: The Cleveland Browns are a shambles. The situation surrounding Deshaun Watson is a mess, and it's frankly incredible he's still in the league. They can no longer rely on Myles Garrett. They seem destined to fail.

Hugh Ferris: I picked the Browns last year and got it wrong. That won't stop me doing it again this year. They're going with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback, which will do little other than prove one more time that it might have been the worst trade (and contract) in NFL history.

Haydn Parry: There seems to be a general consensus that the Miami Dolphins are 'in transition' - which is NFL-speak for 'total rebuild'. They are probably in a race to the bottom with the Arizona Cardinals as things stand.

Joe Bradshaw: Iconic edge rusher Myles Garrett has left the Browns and they still have huge questions at quarterback with Deshaun Watson booed by his own fans during pre-season. Their best hope is a top pick in 2027's stacked-looking draft.

David Brindle: Until now, all of the questions have been tough, but this is easy. After a tumultuous off-season where they moved on from Jaylen Waddle and others, the rebuild is under way for the Miami Dolphins and they face a daunting season.

Ben Collins: Although I'm rooting for British tight end Seydou Traore in his rookie year, this could be a long season for the Dolphins. Their roster looks short on talent having also let Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill go, with Malik Willis entering a season as starting quarterback for the first time.

articles.title: Los Seahawks descorchan la NFL amenazados por Mahomes, Allen, Lamar Jackson y los Rams
articles.standfirst: Seattle abrirá el curso este miércoles ante los New England Patriots en el Lumen Field
articles.summary: Seattle abrirá el curso este miércoles ante los New England Patriots en el Lumen Field
articles.body: La NFL levanta el telón de su temporada 2026 con los Seattle Seahawks como defensores del título y una amplia lista de pretendientes, con el regreso de Patrick Mahomes al frente de unos Kansas City Chiefs hambrientos de revancha, con Lamar Jackson y Josh Allen en busca de su anhelada corona y unos Los Ángeles Rams potenciados con la llegada de Myles Garrett y el regreso del legendario Aaron Donald. Seattle abrirá el curso este miércoles ante los New England Patriots en el Lumen Field, en la revancha del último Super Bowl. Los Seahawks, que conquistaron el segundo título de su historia, pondrán a prueba la continuidad de un proyecto que convirtió una temporada de transición en una carrera triunfal hasta el trofeo Vince Lombardi. La visita de los Patriots a Seattle inaugurará una primera semana con partidos entre el miércoles 9 y el lunes 14 de septiembre, incluidos los duelos Bills-Texans, Ravens-Colts y Broncos-Chiefs, tres citas que medirán desde el inicio las aspiraciones de varios pesos pesados de la Conferencia Americana. Mahomes y los Chiefs llegan después de una campaña sin 'playoffs', una anomalía para la franquicia que dominó buena parte de la última década. Kansas City recibirá a Denver en el cierre de la jornada inaugural, obligado a despejar pronto las dudas alrededor de un equipo que sigue teniendo en su mariscal de campo a uno de los grandes factores diferenciales de la competición. Buffalo y Baltimore salen, una vez más, con Allen y Jackson al frente de sus aspiraciones. Los Bills fueron eliminados en la ronda divisional por los Broncos, mientras que los Ravens ni siquiera alcanzaron la postemporada, dos tropiezos que vuelven a colocar a ambos 'quarterbacks' bajo el foco en la lucha por derribar a los equipos más consolidados de la AFC. Una de las historias de la temporada estará en Las Vegas. Los Raiders iniciarán una nueva etapa con Klint Kubiak como entrenador y el veterano Kirk Cousins previsto como titular, pero toda la atención acompañará a Fernando Mendoza, ganador del Heisman y elegido con el número uno del último 'draft'. El joven mariscal llega tras llevar a Indiana al título universitario y representa la gran apuesta de futuro de una franquicia que busca salir de años de inestabilidad. Los Raiders debutarán en casa contra los Miami Dolphins, aunque el debate sobre cuándo llegará el turno de Mendoza ya forma parte de la actualidad en Nevada. Será otra temporada con dimensión internacional para la NFL, comenzando por el duelo San Francisco 49ers-Los Ángeles Rams fijado en Melbourne este jueves. Madrid recibirá el 8 de noviembre, en el Santiago Bernabéu, el partido entre los Cincinnati Bengals y los Atlanta Falcons, una nueva escala de la expansión global de la liga.

articles.summary: Football is back! college football brought fans a thrilling Week 1 slate over the weekend, and now it's the NFL's turn to take over the sporting world. The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots will kick off the season with a Super Bowl LX rematch on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Football is back! college football brought fans a thrilling Week 1 slate over the weekend, and now it's the NFL's turn to take over the sporting world. The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots will kick off the season with a Super Bowl LX rematch on Wednesday.

Fans will also be treated to a special Thursday game between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers in Australia, a full Sunday slate, and a battle between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football .

While the schedule itself is exciting enough, many fans will look to up the stakes by making a few wagers. Week 1 is always a tricky slate to navigate, but here, we'll pick the best bets based on the early odds from FanDuel Sportsbook .

Will Wednesday's rematch be closer than Super Bowl LX was? Probably. The Patriots were outclassed from the opening kickoff in that one, had no answers for Seattle's relentless pass rush, and went on to lose 29-13.

On paper, New England has a more complete squad this year, and it has a new No. 1 receiver in A.J. Brown. The Seahawks, meanwhile, lost key contributors like Kenneth Walker III, Riq Woolen, Coby Bryant, and Boye Mafe.

Considering how the last meeting went, though, this is a surprisingly small line. Seattle still has the bones of an elite defense, which is probably the biggest issue for New England in this matchup. Brown should give Drake Maye a more reliable top target than he had in Stefon Diggs, but finding time to push the ball downfield will still be a challenge.

And while the Patriots have plenty of talent on their own defense, they're unlikely to corral the Seahawks for a full four quarters in Seattle. Both teams may be able to avoid the dreaded Super Bowl hangover this season, but I'd expect New England to come out of this one with a headache.

Sunday's matchup between the Chicago Bears and Carolina Panthers will be a battle between defending divisional champions. However, these two teams are not equal.

Carolina won the NFC South with a losing record and was fortunate to overcome an offense that ranked just 27th in yards and points and an average (16th in yards allowed) defense.

Good complementary football did allow Carolina to upset the mighty Los Angeles Rams in 2025, but the Panthers got to eight wins by beating up on teams like the New York Jets, Miami Dolphins, and Atlanta Falcons (twice).

The Bears had their fair share of defensive issues in 2025, but they also featured a potent offense led by Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift, Luther Burden III, and Colston Loveland. Head coach Ben Johnson is looking to push that offense a step forward in 2026.

"I want to have the highest-scoring offense ever," Johnson said, per The Athletic's Dan Pompei .

While Chicago's offense might not be historically good this season, it's hard to envision Bryce Young and the Panthers keeping pace in Week 1.

The Las Vegas Raiders stunned the Patriots with a Week 1 win last season—though it wasn't viewed as a major upset at the time. With a new head coach in Klint Kubiak and a seasoned quarterback in Kirk Cousins, the Raiders won't shock anyone with a home win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday.

Kubiak knows what it takes to build a Super Bowl contender, and Cousins will provide the sort of steady presence that Las Vegas lacked a year ago. The Dolphins, meanwhile, have a roster largely devoid of proven talent.

There's a reason why Miami claimed a whopping seven players off waivers during final roster cuts. Why isn't this line even larger, again?

Quarterback Malik Willis is the wild card that could keep Miami competitive in this one. He showed glimpses of being a top-tier dual-threat as the Green Bay Packers backup, and Las Vegas doesn't exactly feature an elite defense. Willis and De'Von Achane could potentially control the game on the ground and give the Dolphins a chance—and Ashton Jeanty's ankle sprain is another obvious factor.

Still, the Raiders will have a massive home-field advantage here and should cover.

articles.title: Week 1 Waiver Wire Top Fantasy Pickups and Drops on Yahoo, Sleeper
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL regular season will begin with Wednesday night's Super Bowl LX rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots. From there, Week 1 will be off and running, and fantasy matchups will be underway.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL regular season will begin with Wednesday night's Super Bowl LX rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots. From there, Week 1 will be off and running, and fantasy matchups will be underway.

While many fantasy managers opt to ignore the waiver wire ahead of Week 1, that quite often means leaving value on the proverbial table.

Depending on when your draft took place, there's a good chance that the landscape has changed enough to justify making a few drops and adds ahead of Week 1. In some cases, making pre-Week 1 moves may be absolutely necessary.

Here, we'll examine our favorite wire targets and drop candidates for point-per-reception (PPR) leagues on Yahoo and Sleeper.

All roster information is according to FantasyPros .

Add: Daniel Jones, QB, Indianapolis Colts

Managers without a high-end backup and/or those looking to stream at quarterback should take a flier on Daniel Jones ahead of Week 1. The Indianapolis Colts' signal-caller is healthy and should put up solid numbers against a Baltimore Ravens defense that was awful in 2025.

Yes, Baltimore's defense should be improved under new head coach Jesse Minter. However, Jones should still remind fans that he was a strong fantasy option before last season's Achilles tear—he finished as QB17 despite appearing in only 13 games.

If Jones does impress in Week 1, he'll be hard to pluck off the waiver wire for anyone low in the pick order. Right now, he's only rostered in 15.8 percent of fantasy leagues.

Drop: Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants

Tyrone Tracy Jr. saw a reasonable role with the New York Giants in 2025, especially after Cam Skattebo suffered a season-ending ankle injury. He topped 1,000 scrimmage yards, finished as RB28, and was a decent streaming flex option for managers in larger leagues.

However, Tracy can be dumped heading into Week 1. Following a series of preseason miscues, he is no longer the clear-cut RB2 behind Skattebo, who is healthy. Tracy is listed on the Giants' depth chart among a group of backups that includes Devin Singletary and recent addition Najee Harris.

It could require multiple injuries for Tracy to see the sort of workload he had a year ago. He's only rostered in 6.3 percent of fantasy leagues, but anyone who did take a late-round chance on Tracy should look for other depth options.

Add: Tyler Allgeier, RB, Arizona Cardinals

Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love was an early draft target in most formats this summer. However, Tyler Allgeier is actually listed as the starter on Arizona's depth chart . Even after Love takes over the RB1 role, Allgeier should have some solid flex value as a committee back.

It could be a few weeks before Allgeier loses his grasp on the starting job, too. Love is recovering from an ankle sprain and, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , is only about "50/50" to even play in Week 1.

Allgeier's fantasy value will likely decline as Love gets healthy and becomes more of an offensive focal point. However, he's worth picking up now and is rostered in only 21 percent of leagues.

When healthy in 2023 and 2024, Houston Texans receiver Tank Dell was a strong flex option, especially in PPR leagues. He averaged 3.9 catches and 55 yards per game and scored 10 touchdowns during that span.

Unfortunately, Dell is still recovering from a very significant knee injury—one that included a torn ACL, MCL, and LCL—that he suffered in December of 2024. He'll open the season on injured reserve, meaning he'll miss at least the first four games of 2026.

Dell will likely miss more than four games, too, as the Texans are unlikely to throw him right back into action once he's cleared to play. And once he is back in the lineup, it could be quite some time before he regains his pre-injury role or form.

Dell is rostered in 13.3 percent of leagues, but it's not really worth stashing him right now in the off chance that he can provide minor midseason value.

articles.summary: The opening week of the NFL season is always exciting. It can also be a difficult one for bettors to dissect.
articles.body:
The opening week of the NFL season is always exciting. It can also be a difficult one for bettors to dissect.

We rarely know exactly what to expect from every team coming out of the preseason, especially when many teams opt to rest their starters. We don't know which teams are poised to regress yet, or which are positioned for a breakthrough.

Sloppy play is also often a hallmark of Week 1, which is how results like last year's Las Vegas Raiders win over the Patriots occur.

While the uncertainty can lead to some big whiffs, it can also yield favorable lines that can be exploited. We'll examine some of our favorite Week 1 odds, from FanDuel Sportsbook , here.

The Buffalo Bills are being heavily hyped heading into Week 1, possibly due to the team's head-coaching change and the arrival of wideout D.J. Moore.

The presence of Josh Allen is obviously a factor, too.

However, the Houston Texans have no business being home underdogs against Buffalo in Week 1. Houston had the league's top-ranked defense a year ago and looks to be even better this season, at least on paper.

Should the Texans trust C.J. Stroud to go play-for-play against Allen? Of course not, but if their defense is close to midseason form, a little smart game management should be enough to get the win.

Houston won this matchup by four points last November. Unless former coach Sean McDermott was truly and significantly holding back Buffalo's offense, the rematch should yield a similar result.

Let's get the obvious out of the way. This is a massive line for a road team playing in Week 1. If it didn't involve Jim Harbaugh, one of the most buttoned-up coaches in the league, I'd probably suggest avoiding it.

However, the Los Angeles Chargers are mostly healthy, they'll be well-prepared for the regular season, and they should be more offensively potent under new coordinator Mike McDaniel.

Against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranked 27th overall a year ago, McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert should put on a show.

The Cardinals do have some serious offensive firepower of their own. However, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is still recovering from an ankle sprain, and L.A. has one of the top defensive rosters in the NFL. Could the Cardinals still surprise? Of course, but it's more likely that this game turns into the rout of the week.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson played through multiple injuries in 2025, while Indianapolis Colts signal-caller Daniel Jones suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. When the two were healthy, though, they were two of the most potent playmakers in the NFL.

Both Jackson and Jones are healthy now, and fans should expect to see some offensive fireworks in this matchup. They should also expect to see a good amount of points on the scoreboard.

The Ravens were atrocious defensively last season, and while new head coach Jesse Minter should spark improvements in 2026, Baltimore's defense probably won't be elite right out of the gate. The Colts, meanwhile, have added some pieces to a defense that ranked 23rd overall last season. However, they are also unlikely to lead with their defense in Week 1.

Between Jackson, Jones, Derrick Henry, and Jonathan Taylor, there's simply too much big-play ability in this matchup to ignore.

articles.title: Patriots make Christian Gonzalez NFL’s highest-paid cornerback with historic $135 million deal
articles.summary: The Patriots made Christian Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history with a four-year, $135 million extension.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots refused to let their most important contract negotiation follow them into the regular season. New England agreed to terms with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez on a four-year, $135 million extension that includes $102 million guaranteed, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Monday night. The deal makes Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. ( espn.com )

"THANK YOU LORD! PATS NATION LETS GO," Gonzalez wrote, according to ESPN .

The announcement ends months of negotiations and ensures that one of the NFL's best young defensive players will remain a foundational piece of the Patriots' long-term plans.

Christian Gonzalez resets the cornerback market

Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon briefly owned the NFL's largest cornerback contract after agreeing to a four-year, $132 million extension with more than $101 million guaranteed in August.

Gonzalez's new deal surpasses both numbers.

The contract carries an average annual value of $33.75 million, edging Witherspoon's $33 million average. Gonzalez and Witherspoon are represented by the same agent, Reggie Johnson, which made Seattle's agreement particularly relevant during New England's negotiations.

The timing creates an interesting backdrop for the beginning of the season. New England will face Seattle at Lumen Field on Wednesday night, meaning the NFL's two highest-paid cornerbacks will be on opposite sidelines immediately after their record-setting extensions.

More importantly for the Patriots, the agreement eliminates a potentially significant distraction before their season opener. Gonzalez had remained with the team throughout negotiations, but uncertainty surrounding his future had become one of New England's biggest preseason storylines. He previously acknowledged his frustration with the process while maintaining that he intended to focus on football.

The Patriots selected Gonzalez with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft after he emerged as one of the class's most talented defensive prospects at Oregon. A shoulder injury ended his rookie season after only four games, but the shortened debut did little to slow his rise.

Gonzalez returned in 2024 and established himself as one of the league's premier coverage defenders, earning second-team All-Pro honors. He followed that performance with his first Pro Bowl selection in 2025 while helping New England reach the Super Bowl.

The 24-year-old recorded 69 tackles and 10 passes defensed across 14 regular-season starts last year. He elevated his production during the Patriots' postseason run, finishing four playoff games with 19 tackles, seven passes defensed, one interception, one sack and one forced fumble.

Those numbers only partially explain his value.

Gonzalez possesses the size, speed and coverage versatility required to follow an opponent's top receiver. His presence gives head coach Mike Vrabel and the Patriots' defensive staff greater freedom to design pressure packages and provide help elsewhere in the secondary.

Shutdown cornerbacks are expensive because they change what a defense can attempt. New England just paid Gonzalez accordingly.

Gonzalez deal sends a larger message about Patriots' future

The Patriots traditionally have been reluctant to allow negotiations to reach the very top of the market. This agreement represents a different approach.

Rather than risk damaging the relationship with one of their best homegrown players, the Patriots paid Gonzalez before another season could push his value even higher. They also prevented future trade speculation from becoming a recurring storyline. The deal is a major investment, but Gonzalez is exactly the type of player a rebuilding organization should prioritize. He is young, proven, plays a premium position and already has demonstrated that he can perform against elite competition.

New England's roster remains centered around quarterback Drake Maye on offense and Gonzalez on defense. Both players now offer the Patriots something every franchise needs: a legitimate star around whom an entire unit can be constructed. Negotiations occasionally appeared capable of producing an uncomfortable ending.

Instead, the Patriots delivered the largest cornerback contract in NFL history and secured Gonzalez through the most important years of his career. The price was historic. Letting Gonzalez eventually leave would have been considerably more difficult to explain.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs to face player No. 4 of the 'NFL Top 100' in 2026
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs to face player No. 4, Los Angeles Rams Quarterback Matthew Stafford, from the 'NFL Top 100' in 2026 | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
The "NFL Top 100 Players" is an annual NFL offseason tradition. There are a few names from the Kansas City Chiefs expected to make the cut, but there are also many opponents featured in this year's rankings. Player No. 4 is a player they are scheduled to face this coming season.

No. 4 is Los Angeles Rams Quarterback Matthew Stafford.

articles.summary: The Super Bowl champion Seahawks are being hunted by the Rams, the team they beat in the NFC championship game. The Rams are building what some call a Super...
articles.body:
The NFL , like most leagues, has a long history of bitter rivals, going way back to Green Bay-Chicago, and progressing through Dallas-Washington, Pittsburgh-Baltimore, New England-Indianapolis, and more recently, Kansas City-Buffalo. And there are plenty more.

But what we have brewing on the West Coast could be just as tasty.

The Super Bowl champion Seahawks are being hunted by the Rams, the team they beat in the NFC championship game. The Rams are building what some are labeling a Super Team. L.A. has added to an already stacked offense by trading for Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, and cornerback Trent McDuffie and welcoming back a three-time DPOY, Aaron Donald.

And none of this was lost on the Seahawks. Safety Nick Emmanwori trolled the Rams after Donald's return with a four-word post that read: "All that for us," and included a pair of sarcastic emojis.

The Seahawks are not resting after winning their second Lombardi Trophy. Perhaps feeling a bit pressured to respond to the Rams and take a risk, Seattle signing troubled cornerback Terrion Arnold, released by the Lions after being arrested on eight felony charges.

All of which should make for a doozy of a race in the NFC West. The problem is the schedule. The NFL made sure this rivalry would receive the longest build-up in history by scheduling their first meeting Christmas Day. They see each other for the second time two weeks later - on the last day of the regular season.

One more game likely awaits. With any luck, it's three weeks later for the right to play in the Super Bowl.

Until then, we are here to sort out the NFL season with your Super Bowl hopefuls, playoff contenders and the bottom feeders. Teams are mentioned on order of how we rank them.

Bills, Eagles among Super Bowl contenders

The Los Angeles Rams (1) had the best offseason in the league, by far. Garrett, McDuffie and Donald are a huge boost to a defense that was solid, but not great. Add that to the most potent offense in the league with QB Matthew Stafford, WRs Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and RB Kyren Williams, and no wonder the Seattle Seahawks (2) are paying attention.

Seattle's John Schneider, the reigning Executive of the Year, overcame the unavoidable departures that happen when a team wins the Super Bowl by making Jaxon Smith-Njigba the highest paid receiver in NFL history and Devon Witherspoon the highest paid cornerback in NFL history. Remember, winning consecutive Super Bowls is rare. Happened just twice this century.

The list of teams entering the season in the category of Super Bowl or Bust is led by the Buffalo Bills (3) . The Bills took a gut punch in 2025 with finally seeing the one team that has prevented them from playing in the Super Bowl in recent years, the Chiefs, take a nosedive and then watching the Patriots re-emerge and return to the title game.

The Bills are counting on a few changes at the top, including a new head coach (Joe Brady) and defensive coordinator (Jim Leonhard) to help them get over the top. And they still have QB Josh Allen, who always gives them a chance.

The Philadelphia Eagles (4) are hoping for addition by subtraction on offense. Trading A.J. Brown, a three-time All Pro still in his prime, gives QB Jalen Hurts a new No. 1 receiver, DeVonta Smith, and the team less drama. The defense is led by the group that can get to the quarterback and keep teams out of the end zone. But will it all be enough to overcome the Rams and Seahawks in the NFC?

The AFC has a long list of teams capable of extending the Bills' misery, including the team that did it last year, the Denver Broncos (5) . The Broncos likely would have been in the Super Bowl if not for QB Bo Nix being injured in the Broncos overtime win over Buffalo in the divisional round. The Broncos will ride with their defense and giving Nix another weapon in ex-Dolphin Jaylen Waddle helps, too.

The New England Patriots (6) reboot is real with QB Drake Maye's impressive breakout year. Maye now has Brown as a No. 1 target. The Pats need the defense to dominate the way it did last year against a much tougher schedule. Speaking of defense, no team will be more reliant on that side of the ball than the Houston Texans (7) , who roll out a unit led by Will Anderson Jr. and added Jadeveon Clowney for depth. C.J. Stroud cannot crash and burn again on the playoffs if the Texans want to compete.

The Baltimore Ravens (8) and Detroit Lions (9) are two teams whose Super Bowl window is closing, but still showing some light. The Ravens' hopes center around QB Lamar Jackson staying healthy and the defense getting its mojo back after adding edge defender Trey Hendrickson. Like the Ravens, the Lions schedule is very forgiving and their offense is loaded with QB Jared Goff, WR Amon-Ra St. Brown, RB Jahmyr Gibbs and OT Penei Sewell. The pass defense needs to improve.

Finally, we get to the team that entered last year having played in five of the last six Super Bowls, winning three. Needless to say, the Kansas City Chiefs (10) need Patrick Mahomes to be healthy and the defense to improve to resemble what it was during that dominant decade. Injuries also will determine if the San Francisco 49ers (11) have a chance of staying close in a division that includes the Rams and Seahawks. QB Brock Purdy has become pretty relevant, but he was just one key piece to deal with injuries last season. Not to be overlooked are the off-season distractions of the owner's arrest and the head coach's auto accident.

Can Chargers (and Mike McDaniel), Jaguars sneak into playoffs?

Los Angeles Chargers (12) offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is working with Justin Herbert, the QB he should have had in Miami. Herbert is a two-time Pro Bowler who has yet to win a playoff game. Jim Harbaugh hopes McDaniel can help change that. The Cincinnati Bengals (13) have a QB in Joe Burrow who led them to the Super Bowl in 2021, but haven't done much since, missing the playoffs the last three years. The offense is good enough for a Super Bowl contender. The defense probably not.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (14) still believe in QB Trevor Lawrence. Jacksonville upgraded the receiving room and defense, which gives the Jags a chance. Travis Hunter is part of both as a backup receiver and starting left corner. The Dallas Cowboys (15) are going all in, but as talented as the offense is with Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, the defense will not win a championship.

A soft schedule and QB Jordan Love gives the Green Bay Packers (16) the edge in a tightly packed NFC North. The Packers are hopeful All-Pro DE Micah Parsons returns from his knee injury a month into the season. The Packers will have to supplant the Chicago Bears (17) at the top of the division. The Bears traded one of QB Caleb Williams' favorite targets (D.J. Moore) and did not do much to upgrade the offensive line. Look for a regression from last year's 11 wins. The Minnesota Vikings (18) will have something to say about the division. But that depends a lot on QB Kyler Murray, who is getting a fresh start after six losing seasons, in seven years, in Arizona.

The Pittsburgh Steelers (19) have one of the best defensive lines in the NFL. Good thing when you are counting on 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers to lead the offense.

The only reason the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20) have a chance at the playoffs is because somebody has to win the NFC South. The division will keep alive the tradition of sending a below .500 team to the postseason.

The future better be bright (and we're talking Dolphins)

Are the Indianapolis Colts (21) the team that started last season 8-2 or finished 0-7? And although that partly depends on the health of QB Daniel Jones, the answer probably is somewhere in the middle. The Washington Commanders (22) went from 12 wins in 2024 to 5 last year. QB Jayden Daniels suffering an elbow injury did not help. Although Daniels appears to be the future, he needs help and losing LT Laremy Tunsil for a good portion, if not all, of the season to a torn triceps is a big blow. The Carolina Panthers (23) made the playoffs at 8-9 last year. Again, the NFC South. So, there always is a chance.

The New York Giants (24) are counting on new coach John Harbaugh to save them. The problem is he has a QB in Jaxson Dart, who was pulled for in-game concussions at least five times last year. Lamar Jackson is not walking through that door for Harbaugh. Speaking of injury prone QBs, the Atlanta Falcons (25) brought in Tua Tagovailoa as insurance for Michael Penix, who is coming off a serious ACL injury. RB Bijan Robinson can only do so much.

The New Orleans Saints (25) have very little going for them other than they are in the NFC South. Have we said the NFC South is bad? For the Las Vegas Raiders (27) , this entire season is about what is best for QB Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in 2026. That is why Kirk Cousins was brought in to mentor and hold down the position until Mendoza is ready. The Tennessee Titans (28) are going to have to find out if their former first overall pick in 2025, QB Cam Ward, is the answer. The former Miami Hurricane struggled mightily in his rookie year.

For the New York Jets (29) , who brought in QB Geno Smith to improve a dreadful passing game, the only hope is in a slew of future draft picks, including three in the 2027 first round. All you need to know about the Cleveland Browns (30) is they named Deshaun Watson the starting QB and traded reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett.

The outlook for the Miami Dolphins (31) was pretty dismal, and then we saw them play three preseason games. Now, it's even worse. The Arizona Cardinals (32) will turn to QB Carson Beck, the third-round pick from Miami, at some point during the season to replace career backup and journeyman Jacoby Brissett, the former Dwyer standout.
